perf.title: Performance profiles
perf.intro: Each profile sets the controller's power mode, fan curve, CPU turbo and frequency caps, GPU clock and display refresh rate all at once. You can see the effect in the live readings below.
perf.refreshToo: Let profiles change the display refresh rate too
perf.factoryHint: Factory state: Entertainment mode, automatic fan, Balanced power plan.
perf.acOnlyTag: Plugged in only; Performance is used on battery
perf.appliedPartial: {name} applied; {n} step(s) failed: {steps}. See the Performance tab for details.
fan.intro: The curve runs on the embedded controller, so it stays in effect even when the app is closed. The first point (45 °C) and the last point (100% at 100 °C) are fixed by the controller; no curve can turn cooling off completely. Thermal protection: if the CPU stays above 93 °C or the GPU above 87 °C for 5 seconds, the fans fall back to the factory table, and the curve returns once things cool down.

set.langHint: In automatic mode, the language follows your Windows country or region setting. The window reloads in the new language when you change it.
set.adminOn: The service is running as administrator. Every profile step is applied, including the GPU clock lock.
set.adminTask: The administrator task is installed, but the service is running with standard privileges. The button below restarts the service as administrator.
set.adminNone: The GPU clock lock in the quiet profiles needs administrator rights. Set it up once, and the service will start as administrator from then on without a UAC prompt.
set.adminAsk: Windows will ask for administrator permission. If you approve, the service restarts as administrator.
set.adminNoRestart: The service didn't restart. Please reopen the app.
set.autostart: Start in the background with Windows
set.startupHint: Your last selected profile is reapplied at startup, since the controller resets some settings on reboot.
set.engineHint: When it's stopped, the profile, fan curve and keyboard stay as they were. Live readings, auto switching and thermal protection stop.
set.quitDone: Service stopped. You can close this window.

mode.sabit.desc: The first color in the palette stays lit.
mode.nefes.desc: The light slowly fades in and out, moving to the next palette color with each breath.
mode.gecis.desc: Smoothly blends between the colors in the palette.
mode.gokkusagi.desc: Cycles through the full color wheel.
mode.nabiz.desc: A double pulse like a heartbeat, with the next color on each beat.
mode.ses.desc: Reacts to your PC's audio output: first color when quiet, last color when loud.
mode.sistem.desc: Follows the value you pick: first color when low, last color when high.
mode.ekran.desc: Mirrors the dominant on-screen color on the keyboard.
err.lenovoNo: not available on this Lenovo model
err.lenovoCustomOnly: on Lenovo a custom fan curve only applies in Custom power mode; Lenovo's own table is driving the fans now
unsup.kbLenovo: No 4-zone keyboard light this app can control was found on this Lenovo. The app sends no commands to the keyboard.
unsup.kbSpectrum: This Legion has a per-key RGB (Spectrum) keyboard. There is no documented single command to paint all keys one color, so the app sends no commands to the keyboard; Lenovo Vantage or the Fn keys keep controlling the light.
unsup.kbOther: This computer's keyboard light is not supported. The app sends no commands to the keyboard.
fan.introLenovo: Lenovo Legion: fan speed and temperatures are read from Lenovo's embedded controller. Profiles switch the power mode (Quiet, Balanced, Performance) and that mode's factory table drives the fans. A custom fan curve is only written while the machine is in Custom mode. Heat protection: if the CPU exceeds 93 °C or the GPU 87 °C for 5 seconds, fans return to the factory table.
lenovo.title: Lenovo Legion
lenovo.hint: The power mode changes with the profiles (Quiet, Balanced, Performance). A custom fan curve is only written in Custom mode; in other modes Lenovo's table drives the fans.
lenovo.reboot: GPU mode changed; restart the computer for it to take effect.
lenovo.fail: Could not change the Lenovo setting: {err}
prof.tam_sessiz.desc: Turbo off, controller in Quiet mode (CPU locked at ~15 W). Fans stay at minimum speed up to 70 °C. GPU locked at 600 MHz, display at 60 Hz. Measured with all 12 threads at full load: 15 W, 59 °C, fan 29%. GPU at full load: 600 MHz, 19 W (65 W unlocked). For reading, writing, movies and late nights.
prof.sessiz_kullanim.desc: Turbo on, but P-cores capped at 2.4 GHz and E-cores at 1.6 GHz, cutting off the most expensive slice of speed. Twice as fast as Silent and still calm. Measured at full load: 24 W, 69 °C, fan 39%. GPU capped at 1100 MHz: 24 W at full load. For browsing, coding, office work, meetings and light gaming.
prof.sessiz_oyun.desc: GPU locked at 1500 MHz: Ampere's efficiency sweet spot, where most of the power draw is cut while FPS drops only slightly. CPU capped at P 2.8 / E 2.0 GHz, with game threads steered to the P-cores. Measured with the CPU at full load: 32 W, 73 °C, fan 50% (uncapped it was 45 W and fan 78%). GPU at full load: 34 W, half of the unlocked 65 W, while clocks stay at 78%.
prof.performans.desc: Controller in Performance mode (highest power limit), no caps, aggressive turbo, GPU unlocked. Fans follow the controller's own performance table. Measured at full load: 61 W (74 W in the first seconds), 98 °C, fan 100%.
prof.ultra.desc: Everything in Performance, plus: fans kick in at 50 °C and reach 90% at 62 °C, so GPU heat is dumped before it builds up in games. EPP 0, core parking off, PCIe power saving off: lowest latency, but high power draw even at idle. Honest measurement: with CPU and GPU both at full load it matches Performance (GPU ~70 W / 1960 MHz, CPU ~32 W); that's this chassis's ceiling. The only differences are the latency tweaks and the earlier fan ramp. Plugged in only; drops to Performance on battery.
msg.batteryUltra: You're on battery: Performance was applied instead of Ultra Performance.
guard.hot: Temperature high: fans temporarily handed back to the controller.
err.dll: InsydeDCHU.dll not found. Put it at lib\InsydeDCHU.dll in the app folder, or install Control Center.
err.noEc: not available on this computer (embedded controller library InsydeDCHU.dll not found)
hw.title: Hardware
hw.intro: The parts in this computer and their live state. Models are read once at startup, measurements refresh every second, disk health every 30 seconds.
cpup.title: Processor
cpup.intro: Only the settings that actually affect this processor model are shown. Everything goes through the Windows power plan; no driver is installed.
cpup.noPL: Power limits (PL1/PL2) and undervolting are not here: they need a kernel driver to write CPU registers. On laptops, the profiles in the Performance tab set the power limit.
cpup.note: Settings are written to the app's power plan. Applying a performance profile replaces them with the profile's values.
cpup.otherScheme: Another power plan is active right now; the first change activates the app's plan.
cpuset.boost.desc: Off: the CPU never goes above base clock, heat and fan noise are minimal. Efficient: turbo only when needed.
cpuset.epp.desc: 0 is the fastest response, 100 the most saving. With Speed Shift the CPU picks its own clock; this value steers that choice.
cpuset.fmax_p.desc: Highest clock of the performance cores. Cutting the most expensive last 15% lowers heat a lot and speed a little.
cpuset.fmax_e.desc: Highest clock of the efficiency cores.
cpuset.fmax.desc: The highest clock the CPU may reach.
cpuset.pmax.desc: Cap as a percentage. 99% is the old way to disable turbo; 100% is unlimited.
cpuset.pmin.desc: Lowest clock percentage at idle. Raising it speeds up response and increases idle power.
cpuset.sched.desc: Scheduler policy on hybrid CPUs. P preferred for games and builds, E preferred for battery.
cpuset.sched_short.desc: The same policy for short-lived threads.
cpuset.park.desc: How many cores may sleep at idle. 100%: no core sleeps (lowest latency, more power).
nvp.title: NVIDIA
nvp.intro: The most used 3D settings from the NVIDIA Control Panel. Changes go to the driver's global profile, which the Control Panel shows too. Per-game profiles are untouched.
nvp.none: No NVIDIA graphics card was found in this computer.
nvp.noApi: The NVIDIA driver (nvapi64.dll) could not be loaded; settings cannot be read.
nvp.adminNote: Changing settings needs admin mode (Settings tab).
nvp.sleeping: The card is asleep: it is not woken, to save battery and heat.
nvp.clockDesc: The highest core clock the card may reach: the setting that cuts heat and noise most. Applying a profile uses the profile's cap. Needs admin mode.
nv.power.desc: Normal: the card lowers its clock when idle. Prefer maximum performance: the clock never drops while a game runs; more heat.
nv.lowlat.desc: On: the driver queues at most one frame; input lag drops, FPS may dip slightly when GPU-bound.
nv.vsync.desc: Fast: no tearing and no frame rate cap; good for older high-FPS games.
nv.fps.desc: Stops the card rendering frames nobody sees: less heat, noise and power. Slightly below the display refresh rate is a good choice.
nv.texq.desc: Performance settings blur distant textures slightly; the FPS gain is small on modern cards.
nv.thread.desc: Spreads driver work across several cores in OpenGL games.
nv.optimus.desc: Which GPU runs apps on a laptop. High-performance NVIDIA wakes the card for every app: shorter battery life.
err.nvSession: Could not open an NVIDIA driver session
err.nvRead: Could not read NVIDIA driver settings
err.nvAdmin: This NVIDIA setting needs admin mode (Settings)

set.adminUntrusted: Administrator mode is only available in the version installed to Program Files with setup.exe. An administrator task installed from any other folder would let every program that can write to that folder gain administrator rights without a UAC prompt.
err.notClevo: not available on this computer (not a Clevo/Monster embedded controller)
unsup.title: Not available on this computer
unsup.fan: Fan curves and controller power modes are specific to the Clevo/Monster embedded controller, which this computer does not have. The app sends no commands to the fans or the controller; the computer itself or the manufacturer's app keeps managing the fans. Profiles still apply CPU, GPU and display settings.
unsup.kb: Keyboard RGB lighting is specific to the Clevo/Monster embedded controller, which this computer does not have. The app sends no commands to the keyboard; the manufacturer's app or the Fn keys keep managing the keyboard light.
unsup.dll: The embedded controller was found but its library could not be loaded, so this feature is off: {err}
err.awOpen: not available on this computer (could not reach the Alienware controller: {err}). Run the app as administrator.
err.awNoProfile: not available on this computer (the Alienware controller reports no suitable power profile)
err.awNoTemp: the Alienware controller reports no temperature; the fans were handed back to the controller's profile for safety
err.awKbNone: no RGB keyboard light found on this computer (models such as the Alienware 16 Aurora have a white-only backlight)
err.awKbOpen: could not open the AlienFX keyboard device
unsup.kbAw: Keyboard RGB lighting is not available on this computer: {err}. Fan and power mode control keep working.
fan.introAw: On Alienware the app runs the curve (the controller has no curve of its own): it checks the temperature every second and sets the fan speed. When the app closes, the fans return to the controller's profile. The dashed line is a reference, not a factory table. Thermal protection: if the CPU stays above 93 °C or the GPU above 87 °C for 5 seconds, or the temperature can't be read, the fans go back to the controller.
msi.title: MSI settings
msi.intro: Settings are written to the embedded controller through MSI's own ACPI-WMI bridge (MSI_ACPI); no extra driver is installed. Writing is enabled only on models with a recognized firmware.
msi.chargeHint: The battery charges up to this percentage and starts charging again 10 points below it. Extends battery life on a laptop that stays plugged in.
msi.roNote: For safety nothing is written to the controller on this computer; only temperatures and fans are read.
msi.fail: Could not apply the MSI setting: {err}
msi.unsupFan: Safe access to the embedded controller could not be established on this MSI computer. The app sends no commands to the fans or the controller; MSI Center or the computer itself keeps managing the fans.
msi.unsupKb: No supported keyboard lighting device was found on this MSI computer (SteelSeries per-key RGB or 3-zone MSI keyboard). No commands are sent to the keyboard.

msi.noCurve: the MSI controller has no custom fan curve

fan.hpIntro: HP Omen / Victus: the BIOS manages the fans and there is no custom fan curve. Profiles choose the BIOS thermal mode (Quiet, Balanced, Performance); "Maximum" runs the fans at full speed, "Factory" returns to the BIOS table. Temperature and fan speed are read from the BIOS.

acer.fanIntro: Acer Predator / Nitro: the fans follow the selected power mode's own table; instead of a temperature curve you can choose a power mode, maximum speed or a fixed custom speed. On this computer, profiles switch to their power mode instead of a curve.
